limits: Only synthetic metadata and freshly created disposable fakes were tested. No protected production pier was read, copied, imported or operated on; whole-pier health and other historical formats are not asserted.

The service rehearsal covers 0.3.3 to 0.3.4 on the pristine Arch/Omarchy Linux/AMD64 owner-user stack, not remote upgrades, other distro runtime installations or power cuts. Earlier releases follow the documented intermediate paths to 0.3.3.

Real QML upgrade buttons use an exact-program guest-only polkit rule, not human password entry. The initial setup receipt is reconstructed from genuine previous-version installer and SSH-enrollment evidence.

The guest loads real sealed desktop archives with harness activation acknowledgements. A separate private native QML test covers hot activation, failed-candidate recovery, preferences and restart; stock Omarchy updater interaction remains manual.

Ordinary-owner storage accounting cannot descend into rootless overlay work directories. Charged usage includes an extra 4 GiB reserve for those unmeasured directories, separately from the 4 GiB guest scratch cap; this is not a complete physical measurement.

Import copies/moves preserve metadata as opaque files; no AppleDouble contents are interpreted and metadata does not substitute for required real state. Existing filesystem, ownership, source-change, stopped-source and epoch-format safeguards remain.
Cross-host handoff remains at 100 GB. Existing experimental capability and broader security/privacy review limits remain.
